name: Fitabase
value: Two documented beat-to-beat routes. (1) Garmin API (OAuth, Garmin Connect app) - Enhanced BBI with a per-beat confidence flag, captured at the wrist during sleep, from devices with a gen 4 or later sensor (premium dataset). (2) Garmin SDK - a 2026-07-29 blog post says Fitabase can pull beat-to-beat intervals with the Garmin SDK when participants sync through the Fitabase Engage app instead of Garmin Connect; daytime coverage and sampling for this route are not stated. Also 15-second heart rate, and Garmin Index blood pressure monitor readings (systolic, diastolic, pulse, source).
note: The two routes do not contradict each other. The KB's EBBI article describes only the API route and answers "SDK or API?" with the API; the SDK route appears in the CIRQA blog post, a KB troubleshooting article "Setting up Fitabase Engage for the Garmin SDK" (last updated 2026-04-15, no streams or rates listed) and App Store release notes (version 1.2, "Connect Garmin device directly to the Fitabase Engage app"; 1.3 and 1.4, Garmin SDK fixes). What the SDK route collects outside sleep, at what rate, whether it is Enhanced or legacy BBI, and who can use it are not stated. Corroborated, as all sources are vendor pages.

name: Beiwe and Forest (Onnela Lab, Beiwe Service Center)
value: Raw phone sensor data and logs, downloadable by researchers through the web download page, the Data Download API or Mano. Streams: accelerometer, gyroscope, GPS (optional fuzzing), screen and power state, identifiers, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, call and text logs (Android only), proximity, magnetometer, device motion and reachability (iOS only), plus surveys and audio-survey recordings. The optional Android ambient (continuous) audio stream has been removed from the backend (commit "removes ambient audio", 2026-07-31, on main by 2026-10-19). Call and text logs come only from the lab-distributed Android builds (onnelaLabServer, commStatsCustomUrl); the Google Play build (Beiwe2) has not asked for SMS/MMS or call-log permissions since 2.5.0. Studies set to "production data" restrict downloads to processed output.
note: Phone numbers and Wi-Fi and Bluetooth MAC addresses are hashed on the phone with a per-device key. Power state on iOS is documented inconsistently (profile holds that conflict). Ambient audio: Android 3.1.0 added it (backend defaults were 10 minutes on, 10 minutes off, 44.1 kHz); migration 0150 (generated 2026-07-31) removes the ambient_audio study settings, so the stream is gone from current backends. The Android build.gradle note describing it has not been updated. The Play build also does not prompt for background location (Android 3.1.2). The build split dates from Google's March 2019 policy change.

The device library LICENSE.pdf (SDK License and Evaluation Agreement) limits use to evaluation, testing and potential development, with the same bar on incorporation, and makes commercialization subject to a separate agreement. Commercial License terms are not published. The Python datalogger tool is described as open source but its README licence section is an unfilled placeholder. Whether a deployed research app counts as evaluation and development is not stated; institutional legal review should decide.

name: Movesense
value: No cloud history; data exists only where the researcher streams or downloads it. On-sensor logging is bounded by memory. HR2, HR+ and MD have 384 kB EEPROM used as a ring buffer that overwrites the oldest data. Flash has 128 MB flash that stops writing when full; Movesense says it holds up to five days of single-channel ECG, over four months of heart rate intervals, four days of 26 Hz acceleration or almost 19 hours of 52 Hz 9-axis motion.
note: Two unit discrepancies, neither material. The data storage doc says 386 kB EEPROM where the hardware variants table says 384 kB; the HR2 page gives 3 Mbit, which is 384 kB, so 386 is a typo. The Flash product page says "128 Mb integrated memory" while the specifications page and hardware table say 128 MB; the published logging durations fit 128 MB, so "Mb" is a typo. For heart rate interval logging on Flash the battery must be replaced about once a month.

value: Three overlapping clauses. s.4(a)(iii): training, fine-tuning, developing or improving any AI model, or putting data in a training, evaluation or benchmark dataset, is a Prohibited Use unless Oura gives prior written consent. s.4(d): the Oura API may not be used to develop, train, fine-tune, evaluate, prompt or otherwise provide input to any AI model or platform, and LLM use is permitted only through the MCP Server; no consent route. s.6(g): using User Data to train or improve any AI or ML system is barred and a material breach; no consent route. s.4(c): a user's own consent does not lift any Prohibited Use. Oura may audit for compliance.
note: Resolves the pilot's open note. The repair agent (consent route exists) and the pilot (no route) were each reading a different clause. Oura's written consent lifts s.4(a)(iii) only; s.4(d) and s.6(g) carry no such route, so under this Agreement alone training on API data is not obtainable, and s.4(d) bars even prompting an AI model with API data outside the MCP Server. "AI Model" is defined to include any "machine learning model", which on its face reaches ordinary statistical ML in a research analysis. Whether a separate Research Agreement overrides these clauses is not public. Aggregators are separately barred from passing data to any AI system (s.2(c), s.4(b)(ii)).

name: Sensor Bio (formerly Biostrap)
value: The V2 specification: PPG sampling 50 Hz by default, configurable to 25 or 100 Hz per organization, with up to 100 Hz raw export and a configurable duty cycle; HR at 1-second resolution during active captures and 1-minute averages otherwise; HRV sampled every 2 minutes overnight. Sensor Bio's May 2026 AHA press release says the platform "captures raw physiological signals at 15,000 samples per second". The press wording names no channel, sensor or aggregate, so it cannot be read as a different measure from the text; the two vendor statements conflict as written.
note: Decision on the 15,000 figure: an aggregate across exported channels does not explain it (three PPG wavelengths plus three accelerometer axes at the 100 Hz maximum is 600 samples per second), and the release gives no other basis, so it stays a conflict rather than being reinterpreted. It may be an internal ADC or oversampling rate, but nothing published says so. For study planning, 100 Hz is the documented researcher-facing ceiling. Ask Sensor Bio what the 15,000 figure measures.
